Subject: Sizing request: dedicated capacity for conversational triage (EdgeHealth)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this — EdgeHealth is evaluating dedicated capacity on Redwood for our conversational triage assistant. High-level context: we run a patient-first chat flow that does symptom triage, simple intake, and care routing. We expect a mix of short clarifying prompts and longer summarization outputs.

Initial traffic snapshot (high-level):
- Peak concurrent sessions (per minute window): ~420–480 (P95 ~450)
- Avg requests per session: 2.1 (median)
- Avg user prompt length: 160–200 tokens
- Avg model response length: 280–360 tokens (20% of responses > 600 tokens)
- Typical inter-arrival: morning surge 08:00–10:30 PT (40% of daily traffic), smaller surge 18:00–19:30
- Latency target: P95 < 800ms for interactive flows (we can accept slightly higher for long summaries)
- Privacy: must run in VPC/on-prem for PHI compliance — private deployment likely

Can you help with a capacity estimate (reserved pool + recommended burst capacity) and a short questionnaire so we can provide token samples and real telemetry? I've attached a small token sample export (edgehealth_token_samples.csv) and our current traffic SLA ask.

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Director of Applied AI, EdgeHealth
https://edgehealth.com

Attachments: edgehealth_token_samples.csv (csv, 42KB)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: dedicated capacity for conversational triage (EdgeHealth)

Sara — thanks for the context and the sample. This is the right place to start. A couple of clarifying items will help us avoid over- or under-provisioning:

Quick questions (if you can answer inline that’s perfect):
1) Session definition: does one session equal a single user session that may contain multiple requests, or do you open a new session per conversation turn?
2) Are your long responses (the 20% >600 tokens) generated synchronously in the same path as short replies, or are long summaries batched/async?
3) Do you plan to use streaming (we can reduce perceived latency with streaming) or full-response returns?
4) Cold start tolerance: how important is cold-KV-cache latency vs. warm cache? (E.g., do sessions prefer warm affinity / pinned sessions?)
5) Tokenization: are the token counts pre- or post-tokenizer? If you have tokenizer samples we’ll validate tokenization variance.
6) Desired availability and failover: do you want cross-region fallback or strictly single-region VPC?
7) Pilot timeline / go-live target?

I attached a short sizing matrix that we use to translate token flows and concurrency into node counts; if you can populate the top section (peak-minute tokens/sec, % long responses, desired P95) we’ll run a modeled footprint. We’ll also propose GPU SKU mixes and a recommended burst pool for morning surges.

Next steps: please send answers and the completed redwood-sizing-matrix.xlsx. After we review, we’ll propose a reserve + burst plan and suggest a 30-minute sizing workshop with our infra team (Marissa) and an ops contact (Priyom).

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect — Dedicated Inference
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jul 14, 2026 at 11:03 AM karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
> Sara — thanks for the context and the sample. A couple of clarifying items will help...

Hi Karthik — thanks, answers below inline. I also attached the completed sizing matrix and a small sample of anonymized session logs.

1) Session definition: one session = user conversation (multiple turns). Sessions are sticky for ~10 minutes of inactivity.
2) Long responses: generated synchronously in the same request path. We occasionally spawn a background job for multi-page clinical summaries but 80% of summaries must be interactive.
3) Streaming: yes, we use streaming for long summaries where possible, but client SDKs have mixed support. Planner should assume mixed mode.
4) Cold start tolerance: low — warm cache preferred. We’re open to session affinity or short pin windows (5–15min).
5) Tokenization: counts are after our tokenizer. Token samples attached to help verify differences vs model tokenizer (edgehealth_token_samples.csv).
6) Availability: single-region VPC with cross-region read-only fallback for exceptional outages.
7) Pilot timeline: pilot in ~6 weeks; production in ~12–14 weeks.

Populated matrix: peak-minute tokens/sec = 360k tokens/minute during surge window; % long responses = 20%; percent streaming-capable clients = 55%.

Attachments: redwood-sizing-matrix.xlsx, edgehealth_token_samples.csv

Cheers,
Sara
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: dedicated capacity for conversational triage (EdgeHealth) — proposed footprint & next steps

Sara / team — looping in a short technical readout after reviewing the samples and the completed matrix. High-level recommendations (engineer-friendly):

- Suggested reserved pool: equivalent of 10 H100-class workers (or 12 A100-80GB workers depending on availability). Rationale: modeled sustained peak-minute token rate with 20% long responses and affinity windows yields ~9.2 effective nodes for 95% of minutes; we size reserve up to 10 to cover steady-state headroom and autoscaler granularity.
- Burst pool: additional 3–4 smaller nodes (A10/A30 family or lower-capacity H100 binned instances) for morning surges with automated warm-up policy. Total burst budget suggested: 30–40% of reserve capacity for the 08:00–10:30 window.
- KV cache strategy: recommend session affinity keyed on user_id with 10–15min pin window to keep KV warm during morning surges. This reduces token compute by ~12% in our model.
- Streaming + chunking: enable streaming for long summaries; degrade gracefully to non-streamed long response if the client doesn't support streaming.
- Quantization: we recommend int8 quantization for short-turn generation models (saves ~2.5x memory); keep a float16 variant for long-summarization paths where hallucination risk is higher.
- SLA & fallbacks: single-region VPC with cross-region read-only failover is supported; we'll propose cross-region read-only fallback only for non-PHI operations if you need strict on-prem constraints.

Next steps:
1) Quick 30-minute sizing workshop (we'll bring priors and a simulator).
2) Pilot: 2-week pilot with 2 reserved nodes (right-sized) + burst staging; we instrument token-level tracing and P95 telemetry.
3) Post-pilot: finalize reserved commit (3/6/12 month options) and adjust burst sizing.

I attached a short preflight checklist that we’ll use to scope networking, IAM/KMS, and pilot runbook items. If that looks good, can we schedule the workshop next week? I’ve tentatively proposed Mon 07/20 10:00 PT and Wed 07/22 09:00 PT — which works better?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Dedicated
